transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah… I guess what finally got me to come in is I can’t stop reacting like something bad is happening, even when it’s just normal stuff. Like at work, if a breaker snaps or a tool drops on the floor, I jump so hard it’s embarrassing. Or if somebody walks up behind me and says something, even if they’re not trying to scare me, I just… I come out of my skin.

And it’s not just the jump, you know? Everybody else laughs or moves on, and I’m still standing there with my heart pounding like crazy, trying to act normal. It keeps hammering way after it should’ve stopped. I do installation and repair work, so there’s noises all the time—tools, panels, people moving around—and I feel like my body is constantly getting yanked into panic before my brain can even catch up.

It’s been bad enough that I figured I can’t just keep pretending it’s nothing.
Have you noticed yourself having upsetting thoughts that won’t go away, or feeling like you have to do certain things over and over again to feel better or prevent something bad from happening?

Yeah… I mean, not like I’m counting things or washing my hands over and over or anything like that. But the thoughts, or pictures, yeah. They come in without me wanting them to.

I’ll be doing something completely normal, like loading tools into the truck or checking what I need for a job, and out of nowhere I’ll see that flash in my head again. Or I’ll hear the trainee yelling, just clear as anything, like it’s right there. And it doesn’t feel like just remembering something in the regular way. It’s more like it hits me before I can stop it, and for a second I’m not really where I am. It knocks me sideways.

I try to shake it off, because I don’t want people noticing, but once it’s in my head it’s hard to get back to whatever I was doing. It’s like my body reacts like it’s happening all over again, even if I’m just standing by the truck with a wrench in my hand.
Have you found yourself feeling irritable or angry more often than usual, even about small things?

Yeah. More than I want to admit, honestly.

I feel like I’m walking around mad almost all the time now, even when nothing is really happening. Little things set me off in my head way bigger than they should. Somebody asks me a simple question, or something doesn’t go the way it’s supposed to, and I can feel this heat come up in me like I’m already looking for a fight. I don’t always say it out loud, but it’s there.

And underneath that, it’s not just anger. It’s guilt. It’s like I failed that kid, and I carry that around every minute. I know people aren’t actually staring at me thinking that, but it feels like everybody can see it on me anyway, like it’s written all over my face. So I’m mad, and then I’m mad at myself for being mad, and then I feel guilty all over again. It’s exhausting.
Have you found yourself avoiding certain places, people, or situations because they remind you of something bad that happened, and you’d rather not feel that way again?

Yeah. Yeah, I do that a lot.

I’ll make excuses to not go near certain panels or breakers, especially if they’re the kind that… I don’t know, just look or sound too much like the one from that day. I’ll tell somebody I need to grab a part, or I’ll say I’ve got another work order backed up, or I’ll act like it makes more sense for someone else to check it. Sometimes it’s not even that the job is dangerous right then, it’s just my head connects it, and once it starts, I know I’m going to be stuck with it.

There are job sites I don’t want to go back to. Even driving near certain places, I’ll take a different way if I can get away with it. And talking about it… I avoid that too. If somebody brings up what happened, or asks me if I’m doing okay, I shut it down. I’ll say I’m fine, or I don’t remember much, or I don’t want to get into it. Because if I start picturing it or talking through it, then it’s like I can’t turn it off. It keeps playing in my head, and I spend the rest of the day trying to get back out of it.

So yeah, I avoid a lot more than I probably admit. I just try to make it look like normal work stuff, like scheduling or being busy, but really it’s because I don’t want to feel that again.
